messages:
sam: Heads up 9 — I sketched a tiny "policy suggester" panel that runs when you create a rollout. It ranks fallback options by: expected latency improvement, estimated quality regression, and cost delta. Want quick reactions.

lina: Love the ranking idea. How do you compute "estimated quality regression"?

sam: Short: we run lightweight distillation checks on a small holdout of recent prompts (not storing full prompts for private deployments) and produce a single score 0-100 called "UIQ" (user-impact quality).

lina: Is UIQ human-auditable? We need transparency for customers.

sam: Yes 9. The panel surfaces the top 3 counterexamples (anonymized) and a one-line explanation: e.g., "short-form prompts lose entity precision".

noah: Whoops we should be careful about sampling: some customers want full diff capture for a short window. Add a toggle to request elevated audit (opt-in, SLA checks).

sam: Good call. Default behavior: 5% diff sampling + metadata only. Enterprise toggle can enable 100% diff capture to a separate secure bucket.

priya: UX nit: the panel should clearly separate "soft degrade" (return alt model but preserve response shape) vs "hard degrade" (trim tokens, drop features). Also show what telemetry we'll collect post-fallback.

sam: Agreed. We'll add checkboxes and a tiny visual: soft vs hard and a list of telemetry items (latency, token-count, response-length, top-k-diff).

lina: Can the suggester take quota signals into account? Example: if tenant quota bursts, we might prefer soft degrade to cheaper quantized variant rather than full handoff.

sam: Yes. We already compute a "quota pressure" metric per-tenant. Suggester ranks fallback types with that as a factor.

noah: API shape request: please keep the rollout API minimal. Add `contingency_policy` as an optional object that can either be inline or a reference (policy_id). Controller should not need to know where it came from.

sam: That matches my thinking. We'll accept both and store canonicalized policy at rollout creation time.

priya: Simulation feature request: let us run the suggester's proposed policy against a sampled window of historical traffic and produce a tiny "what-if" chart: switch count, p95 delta, cost delta, and at most 10 sample diffs.

sam: On my list. The simulator will run in read-only mode and produce a checksumed report you can attach to the rollout.

lina: Ops integration: each suggested policy should link to a playbook fragment (pre-populated text describing steps SRE should take if the fallback doesn't help). We should auto-create a short incident template if the fallback triggers > N times in 1h.

sam: We can auto-wire a playbook anchor and populate variables (model id, region, rollout id). Good idea to create an auto-incident if repeated triggers exceed thresholds.

noah: Safety: add "backoff hysteresis" (e.g., require trigger in 3 consecutive windows OR sustained for >X seconds) and a cooldown after switch. Also we should cap the number of auto-switches per hour to prevent oscillation.

sam: Default caps: max 3 auto-switches per hour, checkpoint decision reason for each switch. UI allows operators to raise cap temporarily with justification.

priya: Legal: ensure customers in Private deployments have default off for any prompt snapshotting. For hosted, we need an explicit consent flag for extended diff capture.

sam: We'll make safe defaults per deployment mode and surface consent checks on the suggester flow.

lina: One more: the UI should expose a "confidence" band (low/med/high) for each suggestion so users can eyeball risk. Derive confidence from similarity between holdout prompts and model training distribution + sample size.

sam: Nice. We'll show confidence and a short blurb about its meaning.

ops-bot: FYI: dedicated pool outages last month showed most incidents were resolved by model handoff within 90s. Consider defaulting short cool-downs for dedicated customers.

sam: Thanks Ops signal. I'll make per-deployment defaults and allow team-level policy overrides. I'll drop console mocks + proto diff in the PR and tag y'all.

lina: Quick thumbs: looks good. Please add the simulator and playbook link before we roll to beta.

noah: +1. Also add a compact export of the simulation results (CSV/JSON) for legal/cust requests.

priya: Great work. If we can keep defaults conservative it's safe to ship to a small beta.

sam: Cool 9. Will follow up with PR and mock images.
